suggestions: Say when the simulator writes its live_truth rows, and make it before the first detection is sent. Playwright presses Reveal as soon as an incident closes, and closing happens on heartbeats about 2 s before the simulator exits. If the rows are written at exit, the reveal can race them. If truth is missing for a closed incident, have reveal return a clear error, not an empty verdict.

Every fresh live-mode folder (data/live_mode, data/cache/e2e/live_mode, the live-check scratch folder) starts its clock at 2026-09-01 21:00 with launch counter 0, so all of them derive the same default seed. Sensor track ids hash (seed, key, launch_ms), and key (LIVE/<scenario>/<seed>/<n>) leaves out the actor and the base. So the first returning-prober launch in two folders, one with P1 and one with another prober whose window also opens at 21:00, gets the same sensor_track_id. record_live_flights then overwrites the first row, and an old incident's reveal in the other folder changes. Add the actor and base, or the live-mode folder, to the hash.

Have the launcher pass the API's --config directory to the child, so the world, scoring (idle_close_s) and truth path match the API's. State that `simulate --dry-run` writes no truth and does not reserve the clock: the launcher test runs it from make check, and tmp_config's in-memory paths cannot reach a child process.

Extend the actor-free-log test to error paths too. A child's stderr could carry a message that names the actor (for example a ScenarioError such as 'P3 flies only at ALPHA'), even though the API validates first.
D-180: say how the hobbyist scenario reports a flight that closes before T+45 (no rerun, so no top score). Pick and record a fixed live-check seed once; never change it to pass.
livemode.spec.ts: also reset live data in beforeAll. The e2e live-mode folder persists between runs, so a killed earlier run would leave incidents in 'Live incidents this session'.

test_new_operator_flies_twice_at_two_bases_after_close: also assert that the invented operator's pattern (cw orbit, 260 m, around hq) and its launch offset (45°, 1,400 m) differ from every configured actor, as the block requires. The reveal-words test should check that flight 2's text names flight 1's live incident id.
Keep the string 'live_truth' out of docstrings and comments in api/, live/ and store/, because the extended FORBIDDEN scan matches any text.
summary: Round 2: both blocking issues from review 1 are fixed. D-182 now prints the actor only on an interactive terminal or with --show-actor (the API never passes it), keeps launched-child logs and the API's logs free of it, and adds a test for that. D-177 derives the default seed from the world seed and a launch counter kept in clock.json, with a test. The plan covers every task checkbox: the simulator and feed client, live incidents, the worker, learning, the case memory, every API route including reveal, the Live page with launcher, picker, incident list, reset confirm and reveal card, live check with exits 0, 1 and 2, make live and make live-check, and the docs. Each test bullet has a named test (determinism, ingest validation, incident forming and closing, no look-ahead, learning, reset with verify_chain, the truth scan extended to live_truth, reveal 404/409/verdict, the Playwright speed-20 run, replay specs unchanged). The exit check is mapped command by command to its evidence, with the soft live-check gate per D-063. I spot-checked the code: the functions the plan names exist with the expected shapes (query_at, DtwMatcher, SwarmMatcher.match_flight, compute_result, CandidateBuilder.forget, DuckTrackStore.over, record_incident, propose_matches, track_rows, record_live_flights). The in-progress live modules match the plan: seeded RNG streams, opaque sensor track ids, closed-only learning through the ports, a feed store separate from the read-only history. No rule is broken and no human decision is needed. The remaining points are robustness suggestions.
